The [case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), which presents the original paper, the Multi100 project and the five reanalyses on which every track of the case is built, is the place to start.

This version of the one-day course on the EU-frames case keeps the tools in the foreground: R, the IDE, the Quarto report, data management and version control. The case is the material that the tools work on. It is a claim of the original author (OA) of a paper about how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, which five analysts reanalysed for the Multi100 project, and the target that the R work of the day reaches is the reproduction, to the third decimal, of the result that Multi100 recorded for one of the three analysts whose analyses rest on means of countries or of cells, chosen by you. A short opening on credibility explains why the tools matter, and the day ends with one look at the curve of alternative analyses of the claim, as the reason that readable code matters. The day uses no menu of specifications and no class chart, and nothing is submitted.

The day works on aggregate data only, the country-year panel of the course and two files that the course rebuilt for two of the analysts, and it is taught in the [browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd), which runs R inside a web page with the data in place. Installing R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) is optional, but the IDE and the report are the subject of half the day, so those who have installed the workspace get more from it, and the facilitator demonstrates every step in the workspace for those who have not. The day runs as four parts of ninety minutes, with breaks of thirty, sixty and thirty minutes between them, and several of its steps are things that the class does together, so it needs a facilitator.

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the day](before.qmd) | Open the browser lab once and read the case study; installing R, an IDE and the workspace is optional and recommended. | 1 to 2 hours |
| [Part 1 – Credibility and software](part-1.qmd) | The three Rs, five analysts whose disagreement could be diagnosed because their code runs, and the toolchain layer by layer; then the browser lab runs on every machine. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 2 – R and the IDE](part-2.qmd) | The R tutorial worked live, the IDE in six steps, and a first session on the panel of your own. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 3 – Data management and the reproduction](part-3.qmd) | From sixteen survey files to one panel, the checks that catch slips, and the reproduction of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL to the third decimal. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 4 – The report, version control and archiving](part-4.qmd) | The reproduction in a rendered report, version control, one look at the curve of the claim, and where finished work is deposited. | 90 minutes |
| [After the day](after.qmd) | Where to go next: R, Quarto, Git and GitHub, and the rest of the curriculum. | as you like |

The other two one-day formats on this case put [open science](../eu-frames-one-day-open-science/index.qmd) or the [statistical methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd) in the foreground, and the [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd) builds the data from the raw survey files and reproduces all five analysts.
